title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: stored metadata bodies on the generic data door are served as their type's read projection (#21086)
body:
Fixes #21086

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changes

Stored datasource credentials are now redacted on generic data door reads of the stored metadata tables too.

A `sys_metadata` or `sys_metadata_history` row read through `findData` / `getData` now carries its `metadata` column as the body's type's read projection. That covers `GET /api/v1/data/:object`, `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query`, `GET /api/v1/data/:object/:id`, and anything else that reads through those two methods. The projection is the one every `/meta` read exit serves. It comes from the same `@objectstack/spec/kernel` redactor registry, through `redactMetadataItem`. The door adds no redaction rule of its own: what counts as a credential is still decided only by the type's registered redactor.

- **One seam**, in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts`, beside the read-path redaction it reuses:
  - `redactStoredMetadataRow` / `redactStoredMetadataRows` serve one row (or one read's rows) with the body projected. Every other column is left as the engine returned it.
  - `storedMetadataBodyProjection` reads `type` when a projection names `metadata` without it, so the redactor can be chosen. The served rows then drop `type` again.
  - `storedMetadataBodyGroupingRefusal` is the grouping refusal below.
- **Wired at the three exits** in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: the flat read and the grouped branch of `findData`, and `getData`.
- **Nothing is exported** from the package entry: `dist/index.d.ts` names none of the new helpers.

## Byte preservation, and failing closed

- A body that holds nothing to withhold is returned by reference, so the caller gets the stored bytes. So is every body of a type that registers no redactor. Only a redacted body is re-serialized.
- A body the door cannot judge is omitted rather than served. There are two cases: a body whose row carries no `type`, and a body that does not parse while its type registers a redactor.
- Objects outside the two tables are untouched, including an object with its own `metadata` column.
- Internal readers of `sys_metadata` read through the engine rather than through this door, so they keep reading the stored body.
- No write-path inverse is owed. `sys_metadata`'s `apiMethods` admit no write verb on this door, and `sys_metadata_history` is append-only, so a redacted body read here can never be written back.

## The grouping refusal, and the Clause-② re-judgement

A `groupBy` entry that names `metadata` on either table is refused with `400 INVALID_FIELD`. The refusal is located at the entry: `groupBy[i]`, or `groupBy[i].field` for the object form. It says the query was not run, and names the route: group by `type`, `name` or another scalar column, and read the bodies with a plain list.

A group key stands for every row that shares it, and the redactor is chosen per row by `type`. So the key cannot be projected without changing which rows it counts. This is the same reason the engine refuses to aggregate a credential field. Every other grouping on these tables is served as before, and so is the same grouping on any other object.

The claim's line was `Clause-②: no`. The grouping refusal removes one accepted query shape from a published door, so it is re-judged here as `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The changeset is `minor` under the launch-window convention, and carries the `adr-0087` disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The row projection itself changes served values only, not what the door accepts.

## Tests

All readings are at `a375e4e9a` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), after a merge of `main` at `fed0db8f`, unless noted.

- **New suite** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.data-door-stored-metadata-redaction.test.ts`: 17 passed. It pins both halves:
  - **withheld**: list, by-id, `select=metadata` on both reads, version snapshots, an already-parsed body, and a stand-in redactor for another type (the door follows the registry);
  - **preserved**: stored bytes for clean bodies, other columns, exactly the named projection, objects outside the set, other groupings;
  - **refusal**: both entry forms on both tables, with `code` / `status` / `param` / `field` asserted and `engine.aggregate` never called.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`**: `vitest run` gave 197 files passed, 3 skipped; 2948 tests passed, 19 skipped. `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) exits 0, and `--listFiles` includes the new test file.
- **Ablations**, one-time, each run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. In every leg the anchor hit once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven (blob equal to `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty). Each ran at `d64f1487`, before the merge, against the suite as it stood then (the two later suite edits change only the stub engine's guards, not the subject):
  - A1, the list projection removed: 8 of 17 red, all on the withheld side.
  - A2, the by-id projection removed: 2 of 17 red.
  - A3, the grouping refusal removed: 3 of 17 red.
  - P1, clean bodies re-serialized: the byte-preservation pin red.
  - P2, the object scope widened to every object: the two outside-object pins red.
  - P3, the added `type` never dropped: the two projection pins red.
- **Live**: a showcase boot on a fresh database (`objectstack dev --seed-admin`), with credential-bearing datasource rows seeded at rest. After the fix:
  - list, by-id, `select=metadata` and `query` reads of both tables served none of the seeded values;
  - `groupBy: ["metadata"]` answered 400, and `groupBy: ["type"]` answered 200;
  - a credential-free datasource row and a translation row were served byte-identical to their stored column, on both tables.
- **Gates**: derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from the change set itself: 70 commands at `a375e4e9a`, after a full `turbo run build` (72 of 72 tasks). All 70 exit 0. `--ran` reconciles to 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
  - An earlier run on the pre-fix-up tree reddened two gates on the new suite, and both were fixed in the suite. `check:engine-double-contract` flagged an unguarded `findOne` double, and `check:where-matcher` flagged a stub matcher that misread a combinator.
- **Lint**, a proven narrowing: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the three changed TypeScript files reports 3 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. `--print-config` resolves the config for each of them. The config enables no type-aware linting (`parserOptions` carries only `ecmaVersion` and `sourceType`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

## Acceptance notes

- Scope is the generic data door (`findData` / `getData`) for the two stored-metadata tables.
- The datasource doors (`/api/v1/datasources/:name`, `/api/v1/meta/datasource/:name`) are untouched.
- No file of the sibling card's surface is touched (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`).
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains one row for the new suite's `findOne` double, which routes through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`. `check:engine-double-contract` asks for exactly that row.
- Landing is a human floor (security boundary): this PR stays draft for the maintainer.
